key_works: Bluvstein et al. (2024), *Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays*, arXiv:2312.03982.

title: Physically costed qLDPC routing in mobile arrays
open: Implement high-rate code checks with explicit transport time, collision avoidance, cooling, optical access, and correlated-motion errors included.
status: Reconfigurability changes connectivity constraints but does not make movement free.
why: Tests a leading route for realizing sparse nonlocal quantum codes.
key_works: Bluvstein et al. (2024), *Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays*; Bravyi et al. (2024), *High-threshold and low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum memory*.

title: Optical-power scaling of large atom processors
open: Increase array size and active-gate throughput without proportional growth in expensive laser power, intensity instability, scattered light, and cooling demand.
status: Large coherent arrays and rapid replenishment are demonstrated; affordable sustained optical operation is a separate scaling target.
why: Atom count is not the same as economically operable computational capacity.
key_works: Chiu et al. (2025), *Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system*, arXiv:2506.20660.

title: Erasure detection with controlled false-positive and false-negative rates
open: Optimize physical erasure flags jointly with the decoder, including missed losses, false alarms, detection latency, and disturbance from checking.
status: Erasure conversion improves theoretical thresholds, but imperfect flags change both decoding and architecture costs.
why: A supposedly located error is useful only when its location information is reliable.
key_works: Wu et al. (2022), *Erasure conversion for fault-tolerant quantum computing in alkaline earth Rydberg atom arrays*, arXiv:2201.03540.

title: Foundry-scale spin-qubit yield with complete operations
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Achieve reproducible large arrays where initialization, readout, one-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and tuning all meet a common fault-tolerance specification.
status: A 300-mm foundry unit cell exceeding 99% fidelity in all operations is a major partial result, not a complete large-array yield demonstration.
why: Manufacturing compatibility matters only if the full operation set scales.
key_works: Paul Steinacker et al. (2025), *A 300mm foundry silicon spin qubit unit cell exceeding 99% fidelity in all operations*, arXiv:2410.15590.

title: Predictive control of spin-qubit device variability
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Predict and compensate valley splitting, charge disorder, residual isotope effects, and device-to-device control differences without exponentially growing tuning effort.
status: Foundry demonstrations identify concrete residual error mechanisms; uniform autonomous operation across large arrays remains unresolved.
why: Variability can make nominally scalable fabrication operationally unscalable.
key_works: Steinacker et al. (2025), *A 300mm foundry silicon spin qubit unit cell exceeding 99% fidelity in all operations*; Guido Burkard et al. (2023), *Semiconductor spin qubits*.

title: Long-distance two-dimensional coherent spin transport
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Shuttle spin information across a useful two-dimensional network while controlling valley transitions, charge loss, phase accumulation, and spatially varying noise.
status: Coherence-protection results for mobile silicon spins are advancing; short-path preservation is not a complete network demonstration.
why: Could separate storage, interaction, and readout zones without dense local wiring.
key_works: Jan A. Krzywda et al. (2026), *Coherence Protection for Mobile Spin Qubits in Silicon*, arXiv:2602.09179.

title: Error correction with simultaneous spin shuttling
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Execute repeated logical-code cycles while transporting multiple spins, with measured correlated transport errors and scheduling overhead.
status: Mobile-spin coherence results provide ingredients; logical fault tolerance requires the entire transport-and-measurement cycle.
why: Determines whether shuttling reduces architecture cost rather than moving noise elsewhere.
key_works: Krzywda et al. (2026), *Coherence Protection for Mobile Spin Qubits in Silicon*, arXiv:2602.09179; Burkard et al. (2023), *Semiconductor spin qubits*.

title: Fast spin readout at acceptable power and wiring cost
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Jointly optimize single-shot readout speed, assignment error, backaction, multiplexing, and cryogenic dissipation for repeated large-array error correction.
status: Strong individual readout results do not determine a scalable joint operating point.
why: Readout can dominate both cycle time and classical interface complexity.
key_works: Guido Burkard, Thaddeus Ladd, Andrew Pan, John Nichol, and Jason Petta (2023), *Semiconductor spin qubits*, DOI:10.1103/RevModPhys.95.025003.

title: Higher-temperature group-IV spin–photon nodes
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Maintain a useful combination of spin coherence, optical indistinguishability, collection efficiency, and gate fidelity at temperatures that materially simplify cooling.
status: Group-IV color-center models identify phonon-limited tradeoffs; improving one property alone does not establish a complete node.
why: Could reduce the infrastructure burden of solid-state quantum networks.
key_works: Isaac B. W. Harris and Dirk Englund (2024), *Coherence of group-IV color centers*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.109.085414.

title: Deterministic telecom-defect integration in silicon photonics
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Fabricate large arrays of individually addressable telecom emitters with useful yield, frequency tuning, spin control, and low-loss photonic coupling.
status: Electrical manipulation and cavity-array integration demonstrate components; deterministic complete-node yield remains a stronger target.
why: Could exploit mature silicon photonics for quantum interconnects.
key_works: A. M. Day et al. (2024), *Electrical manipulation of telecom color centers in silicon*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-48968-w; *Multiplexed color centers in a silicon photonic cavity array* (2025), Optica 12, 1400.

title: Scalable rare-earth nuclear registers with optical networking
subfield: Semiconductor spins, defects, and rare-earth systems
open: Combine reproducible nuclear-spin registers, high-fidelity local operations, and repeated optical entanglement generation without destroying stored information.
status: Deterministic local registers and Bell-state preparation are demonstrated; a scalable connected computing architecture remains open.
why: Combines long-lived storage with optically accessible interfaces.
key_works: Andrei Ruskuc, Chun-Ju Wu, Jake Rochman, Joonhee Choi, and Andrei Faraon (2022), *Nuclear spin-wave quantum register for a solid-state qubit*, arXiv:2108.12723; DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-04293-6.

title: End-to-end fault-tolerant fusion-based computation
open: Demonstrate sustained logical error suppression and universal computation when source, propagation, switching, fusion, detector, and feed-forward imperfections are combined.
status: Fusion-based architectures and modular photonic systems are established milestones, not a complete fault-tolerant computation demonstration.
why: Tests the full loss budget rather than isolated optical components.
key_works: Sara Bartolucci et al. (2023), *Fusion-based quantum computation*, arXiv:2101.09310; H. Aghaee Rad et al. (2025), *Scaling and networking a modular photonic quantum computer*.

title: Large banks of mutually indistinguishable efficient photon sources
open: Produce many simultaneously usable photons with high collection efficiency, purity, indistinguishability, stability, and manufacturing yield.
status: Excellent individual sources do not establish a complete bank meeting all requirements concurrently.
why: Multiphoton success rates compound source imperfections.
key_works: R. N. Alexander et al. (2025), *A manufacturable platform for photonic quantum computing*, arXiv:2404.17570; DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08820-7.

title: Resource-state factories with bounded multiplexing overhead
open: Produce the required photonic entangled resource states at useful rates while explicitly accounting for probabilistic fusion, buffering, switching loss, and discarded attempts.
status: Resource-state constructions exist; practical factory yield is not specified by asymptotic universality.
why: Factory overhead can dominate the complete optical computer.
key_works: Bartolucci et al. (2023), *Fusion-based quantum computation*, arXiv:2101.09310.

title: Feed-forward and optical delay without excessive loss
open: Integrate detection, decoding, switching, and delay so that photons survive the required classical decision latency with a useful total success probability.
status: Modular demonstrations establish feasibility at selected scales; the joint latency–loss budget remains a scaling wall.
why: Photons cannot simply wait in an ordinary register while a controller catches up.
key_works: Aghaee Rad et al. (2025), *Scaling and networking a modular photonic quantum computer*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08406-9.

title: Wafer-scale photonic loss and yield closure
open: Demonstrate manufacturing distributions in which cumulative propagation, coupling, component, and packaging losses satisfy a complete fault-tolerant architecture’s requirements.
status: Manufacturable photonic platforms are reported; acceptable median component performance does not ensure acceptable whole-system yield.
why: Many small losses multiply across a large optical circuit.
key_works: Alexander et al. (2025), *A manufacturable platform for photonic quantum computing*, arXiv:2404.17570.

title: High-rate detector arrays with computation-grade error models
open: Scale photon-number-sensitive detection while controlling dead time, saturation, dark counts, timing uncertainty, readout heat, and correlated failures.
status: Detector performance must be evaluated inside a repeated computation cycle, not only through isolated efficiency measurements.
why: Detectors are both measurement devices and active components of photonic logic.
key_works: Alexander et al. (2025), *A manufacturable platform for photonic quantum computing*; Aghaee Rad et al. (2025), *Scaling and networking a modular photonic quantum computer*.

title: Unambiguous nonabelian Majorana operations in solid-state devices
open: Demonstrate fusion and braiding behavior with controls that exclude trivial Andreev-state and measurement-artifact explanations in the proposed solid-state platform.
status: Parity-readout demonstrations are not by themselves demonstrations of nonabelian statistics or topological protection.
why: Establishes the physical premise of Majorana-based topological computation.
key_works: Morteza Aghaee et al. (2025), *Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2; Chetan Nayak et al. (2008), *Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation*.

title: Exponentially improving topological-qubit protection
open: Measure the predicted improvement in logical protection as relevant device dimensions increase, while separately controlling poisoning, readout errors, and ordinary calibration improvements.
status: A parity signal or long lifetime alone does not establish the required scaling law.
why: Tests the promised protection mechanism rather than a single favorable device.
key_works: Aghaee et al. (2025), *Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*; Nayak et al. (2008), *Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation*, arXiv:0707.1889.

title: Parity-poisoning control during topological computation
open: Quantify and suppress parity changes during preparation, measurement, coupling, and proposed braiding operations, including correlations between device segments.
status: Static parity measurement does not establish a computation-compatible poisoning budget.
why: Uncontrolled parity changes directly corrupt the encoded information.
key_works: Aghaee et al. (2025), *Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2.

title: A physical universal nonabelian-anyon computing platform
open: Realize a platform with experimentally certified anyons supporting universal protected gate operations, together with initialization, readout, and manageable error rates.
status: Mathematical universality of suitable anyon models does not establish their controllable physical realization.
why: Could avoid some non-topological gate overheads of more restricted anyon models.
key_works: Chetan Nayak, Steven Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma (2008), *Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation*, arXiv:0707.1889.

title: High-fidelity molecular gates beyond motion-sensitive demonstrations
open: Experimentally realize molecular entangling gates whose performance remains high under measured dipole-interaction fluctuations and realistic trap motion.
status: A 2026 proposal predicts resilient controlled-phase gates; its favorable calculated fidelity is not an experimental result.
why: Unlocks polar molecules’ rich interactions and internal structure for computation.
key_works: Yan Lu and Xiao-Feng Shi (2026), *High-fidelity molecular quantum logic gates resilient to interaction fluctuation*, arXiv:2605.19741; DOI:10.1103/5k4z-dgn2.

title: Repeated molecular computation with coupled internal and motional states
open: Maintain accurate gates across long sequences while controlling rotational, hyperfine, motional, and interaction-induced errors in an array of molecules.
status: Two-body gate proposals and molecular entanglement are partial foundations; complete scalable error budgets remain undeveloped.
why: Molecules provide useful structure but also additional error channels.
key_works: Lu and Shi (2026), *High-fidelity molecular quantum logic gates resilient to interaction fluctuation*, arXiv:2605.19741.

title: Strong spin–photon coupling for electrons on solid neon
open: Demonstrate coherent spin–photon coupling strong and clean enough for useful gates or networking, rather than only charge–photon coupling.
status: Electron charge-qubit control and interaction demonstrations do not settle the spin-interface target.
why: Could combine long-lived spin storage with electrically accessible circuit interfaces.
key_works: Y. Tian et al. (2026), *Nb-Ti-N nanowire resonators and prospects for spin-photon coupling with electrons on solid neon*, DOI:10.1103/jq9v-n4rn.

title: Scalable multi-electron computation on solid neon
open: Extend interacting-electron demonstrations into reproducible arrays with initialization, individual control, entangling gates, readout, and a complete correlated-noise model.
status: Two-qubit interactions and gates have been reported; “first interaction” is no longer the open problem.
why: Tests whether a promising low-disorder substrate can support a complete computing architecture.
key_works: Xinhao Li, Yizhong Huang, Xu Han, Xianjing Zhou, and Dafei Jin (2025), *Coherent manipulation of interacting electron qubits on solid neon*, arXiv:2503.23738.

title: Fault-tolerant remote gates with a net architectural benefit
open: Demonstrate remote logical gates whose total error, latency, and resource cost make modular computation preferable to the best local alternative.
status: Physical remote gates and distributed algorithms are demonstrated; useful logical-level crossover remains separate.
why: Establishes whether networking actually helps build a larger computer.
key_works: Main et al. (2025), *Distributed Quantum Computing across an Optical Network Link*, arXiv:2407.00835.

title: Repeater advantage with finite memories and real latency
open: Exceed the appropriate repeaterless benchmark at useful rates after accounting for finite memory lifetime, heralding delay, multiplexing, local gates, and all unsuccessful attempts.
status: Capacity bounds define the target; partial repeater components do not demonstrate the complete rate advantage.
why: Determines whether entanglement can be distributed economically beyond direct-link limitations.
key_works: Pirandola et al. (2017), *Fundamental Limits of Repeaterless Quantum Communications*, arXiv:1510.08863.

title: Heterogeneous quantum-node interoperability
open: Connect different qubit platforms while preserving entanglement fidelity, timing compatibility, frequency conversion, and an auditable end-to-end error model.
status: Individual interfaces and homogeneous links are partial results; interchangeable computing modules remain an integration target.
why: The best memory, processor, and communication qubit may be different physical systems.
key_works: Hai-Tao Tu et al. (2026), *Quantum-memory-assisted on-demand microwave-optical transduction*, arXiv:2509.18834; Main et al. (2025), *Distributed Quantum Computing across an Optical Network Link*.

title: Efficient low-noise microwave–optical transduction
open: Simultaneously achieve useful conversion efficiency, low added noise, sufficient bandwidth, and superconducting-device-compatible heat and magnetic environments.
status: Coherent conversion demonstrations exist; favorable performance in one metric does not close the complete interface budget.
why: Links microwave processors to low-loss optical networks.
key_works: Ujjwal Gautam, Nasser Gohari Kamel, Sourabh Kumar, and Daniel Oblak (2026), *Coherent microwave-to-optical transduction with Yb:YSO spins strongly coupled to a 3D resonator*, arXiv:2609.02226.

title: On-demand transduction integrated with a working processor
open: Couple a memory-assisted on-demand transducer to actual computational qubits and demonstrate repeated entanglement transfer without damaging local computation.
status: Memory-assisted on-demand transduction is demonstrated; processor integration and repeated-operation fidelity remain stronger requirements.
why: Synchronization is as important as conversion efficiency in a distributed computer.
key_works: Hai-Tao Tu et al. (2026), *Quantum-memory-assisted on-demand microwave-optical transduction*, arXiv:2509.18834; DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75752-9.

title: Deadline-aware entanglement routing
open: Route and schedule stochastic entanglement generation so that fidelity, memory expiration, application deadlines, and fairness are jointly controlled.
status: Networking formulations exist; optimal or reliably near-optimal policies under realistic coupled constraints remain unresolved.
why: An available path is useless if its entanglement expires before use.
key_works: *Networking Challenges in Distributed Quantum Computing* (2018), arXiv:1810.08421.

title: Distributed resource-state construction under loss
open: Build multipartite graph or code states across unreliable links with bounded memory, realistic heralding, and a favorable logical-computation rate.
status: Fusion and networking protocols supply primitives; a complete finite-resource distributed construction remains workload-dependent.
why: Multipartite resources can reduce repeated remote-gate overhead.
key_works: Bartolucci et al. (2023), *Fusion-based quantum computation*, arXiv:2101.09310; Aghaee Rad et al. (2025), *Scaling and networking a modular photonic quantum computer*.

title: Cross-layer optimization of distributed quantum applications
open: Optimize compilation, code choice, entanglement generation, routing, and classical control together, with guarantees tied to application success rather than isolated link metrics.
status: Separate networking and compilation solutions do not determine the best end-to-end design.
why: Local improvements can worsen distributed completion time or reliability.
key_works: *Networking Challenges in Distributed Quantum Computing* (2018), arXiv:1810.08421; Main et al. (2025), *Distributed Quantum Computing across an Optical Network Link*.

title: Verified compilation of dynamic quantum programs
open: Extend machine-checked compiler correctness to realistic programs with mid-circuit measurement, reset, classical branching, loops, and resource constraints.
status: Verified optimizers and dynamic assembly languages exist; complete semantic coverage across a production toolchain is not established by either alone.
why: Compiler errors can invalidate physical results despite perfectly functioning hardware.
key_works: Kesha Hietala et al. (2020), *A Verified Optimizer for Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:1912.02250; Andrew Cross et al. (2022), *OpenQASM 3: A broader and deeper quantum assembly language*, arXiv:2104.14722.

title: Verified lowering from logical operations to calibrated pulses
open: Connect formal logical-circuit correctness to pulse-level implementations through explicit assumptions about calibration, crosstalk, leakage, timing, and approximation error.
status: Gate-level verification does not certify the physical meaning of a calibrated pulse sequence.
why: Closes the semantic gap between a proof about software and the experiment actually executed.
key_works: Hietala et al. (2020), *A Verified Optimizer for Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:1912.02250; Krantz et al. (2019), *A quantum engineer’s guide to superconducting qubits*.

title: Portable semantics for cross-device quantum execution
open: Specify portable behavioral contracts for timing, measurement, reset, randomness, and failure reporting without pretending different devices share identical noise or instruction semantics.
status: Common languages help express programs; they do not by themselves guarantee equivalent physical behavior.
why: Enables reproducible software without hiding device-specific assumptions.
key_works: Cross et al. (2022), *OpenQASM 3: A broader and deeper quantum assembly language*, arXiv:2104.14722.

title: Empirically calibrated full-stack resource estimators
open: Build estimators whose predictions of runtime, physical resources, energy, and failure probability are repeatedly checked against executed logical workloads.
status: Detailed resource models exist; predictive calibration across changing hardware and software remains an open infrastructure target.
why: Makes architectural and application claims falsifiable.
key_works: Fellous-Asiani et al. (2023), *Optimizing resource efficiencies for scalable full-stack quantum computers*, arXiv:2209.05469; Gidney (2025), *How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits*.

title: Programmable real-time control with deterministic deadlines
open: Support rich adaptive quantum programs while bounding controller, decoder, and communication latency, including overload and fault behavior.
status: Expressive dynamic languages and real-time experiments are partial foundations; deadline-safe composition remains difficult.
why: A missed feedback deadline can be a physical computation error.
key_works: Cross et al. (2022), *OpenQASM 3*, arXiv:2104.14722; Google Quantum AI (2025), *Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold*.

title: Identifiable context-dependent quantum noise models
open: Determine which noise parameters can be reliably inferred when operations depend on simultaneous gates, history, drift, and hidden device states.
status: Standard characterization models simplify these dependencies; fitting a model does not establish identifiability.
why: Compilation and error correction can fail when the noise model is confidently wrong.
key_works: Timothy Proctor et al. (2017), *What randomized benchmarking actually measures*, arXiv:1702.01853.

title: Certified approximation of resource-optimal quantum compilation
open: Produce useful approximation guarantees for compilation objectives that jointly include non-Clifford count, depth, ancillas, routing, and architecture-dependent errors.
status: Exact optimization is intractable for broad formulations; strong practical heuristics rarely come with complete optimality certificates.
why: Determines whether a reported resource improvement is close to the best attainable implementation.
key_works: Hietala et al. (2020), *A Verified Optimizer for Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:1912.02250; Gidney (2025), *How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits*.

title: Safe adaptive quantum control under drift
open: Learn and update controls online while guaranteeing acceptable exploration cost, avoiding unstable feedback, and preserving a computation’s declared error budget.
status: Parameter tracking is progressing; general safe adaptation during valuable computation remains unresolved.
why: Large systems need continual adaptation without treating running jobs as uncontrolled experiments.
key_works: Berritta et al. (2026), *Real-Time Adaptive Tracking of Fluctuating Relaxation Rates*, DOI:10.1103/gk1b-stl3.

title: Useful regimes of polynomial-cost error mitigation
open: Characterize structural promises on circuits, observables, and noise under which mitigation remains polynomial-cost and scientifically useful.
status: General exponential-overhead lower bounds rule out unrestricted cheap mitigation; the open problem is identifying favorable restricted regimes.
why: Directs mitigation toward settings where it can work in principle.
key_works: Ryuji Takagi, Suguru Endo, Shintaro Minagawa, and Mile Gu (2022), *Fundamental limits of quantum error mitigation*, arXiv:2109.04457.

title: Tight mitigation lower bounds for realistic noise
open: Derive matching lower and upper resource bounds for mitigation under biased, correlated, non-Markovian, and drift-dependent noise models.
status: Strong general limits exist for important models, but do not give a complete physically realistic classification.
why: Prevents spending experimental resources on provably unfavorable regimes.
key_works: Takagi et al. (2022), *Fundamental limits of quantum error mitigation*, arXiv:2109.04457.

title: Reliable zero-noise extrapolation under model mismatch
open: Produce calibrated uncertainty intervals when noise scaling changes the noise mechanism, circuit behavior, or drift trajectory rather than simply multiplying a fixed error rate.
status: Extrapolation methods exist; plausible curve fits do not guarantee valid zero-noise estimates.
why: Prevents systematically biased “corrected” experimental results.
key_works: Zhenyu Cai et al. (2023), *Quantum Error Mitigation*, arXiv:2210.00921; DOI:10.1103/RevModPhys.95.045005.

title: Probabilistic error cancellation with affordable characterization
open: Reduce the complete cost of cancellation, including learning and refreshing the noise model, while certifying residual bias from imperfect characterization.
status: Quasiprobability-based cancellation is established; its sampling and characterization overheads can both be prohibitive.
why: A mitigation protocol cannot assume an exact noise model supplied for free.
key_works: Cai et al. (2023), *Quantum Error Mitigation*, arXiv:2210.00921.

title: Virtual distillation with correlated state copies
open: Establish effective protocols and valid guarantees when nominal copies share drift, preparation biases, or correlated errors.
status: Idealized independent-copy analyses do not cover every realistic repeated preparation.
why: Shared errors can survive or be amplified by nonlinear purification estimators.
key_works: Cai et al. (2023), *Quantum Error Mitigation*, arXiv:2210.00921; Proctor et al. (2017), *What randomized benchmarking actually measures*.

title: Scalable characterization of correlated gate errors
open: Recover the error features most relevant to logical computation with feasible experiments, without assuming that average gate fidelity determines them.
status: Benchmarking metrics capture selected operational quantities; many distinct correlated channels can share similar headline scores.
why: Reliable fault-tolerance predictions require more than one number per gate.
key_works: Proctor et al. (2017), *What randomized benchmarking actually measures*, arXiv:1702.01853; Bausch et al. (2024), *Learning high-accuracy error decoding for quantum processors*.

title: Verification of analog simulation beyond classical tractability
open: Certify scientifically relevant analog-simulation outputs using independent controls, bounds, and cross-platform checks when exact classical simulation is unavailable.
status: Agreement in classically tractable regimes is necessary but does not alone validate the extrapolated hard regime.
why: The most valuable analog results are precisely those hardest to verify directly.
key_works: Joseph Tindall et al. (2024), *Efficient tensor network simulation of IBM’s Eagle kicked Ising experiment*, arXiv:2306.14887; LeBlanc et al. (2015), *Solutions of the Two Dimensional Hubbard Model*.

title: Spoof-resistant interpretation of cross-entropy benchmarks
open: Determine which additional tests make cross-entropy-style scores meaningful evidence of the intended computation against explicitly optimized classical spoofers.
status: A high score on a selected statistic is not equivalent to distributional correctness or useful computational advantage.
why: Prevents benchmark optimization from replacing the task being benchmarked.
key_works: Bouland et al. (2018), *Quantum Supremacy and the Complexity of Random Circuit Sampling*; Andrew Cross et al. (2019), *Validating quantum computers using randomized model circuits*, arXiv:1811.12926.

title: Area law for general gapped two-dimensional Hamiltonians
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Prove an entanglement-entropy area law for ground states of general bounded-locality, uniformly gapped two-dimensional Hamiltonians under appropriate standard assumptions.
status: Open. One-dimensional theorems and special higher-dimensional cases do not establish the general two-dimensional result.
why: Would constrain ground-state complexity and support tensor-network approximations.
key_works: Jens Eisert, Marcus Cramer, and Martin Plenio (2010), *Area laws for the entanglement entropy—a review*, arXiv:0808.3773; Simons Institute (2024), *Quantum Complexity: Quantum PCP, Area Laws, and Quantum Gravity*.

title: Efficient certified contraction of physically promised PEPS
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Identify broad, checkable physical promises under which projected entangled-pair states can be contracted efficiently with rigorous observable-error bounds.
status: Generic tensor-network contraction is difficult; an area law or apparently modest bond dimension does not by itself supply an efficient contraction algorithm.
why: Defines the classical boundary against which quantum simulation must compete.
key_works: Eisert, Cramer, and Plenio (2010), *Area laws for the entanglement entropy—a review*; Tindall et al. (2024), *Efficient tensor network simulation of IBM’s Eagle kicked Ising experiment*.

title: Asymptotic stabilizer rank of magic-state tensor powers
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Determine tight asymptotic exact and approximate stabilizer-rank growth for tensor powers of important resource states such as the T state.
status: Decomposition algorithms and lower bounds leave substantial uncertainty in the optimal exponential behavior.
why: Controls a major family of classical simulation algorithms for non-Clifford circuits.
key_works: Sergey Bravyi and David Gosset (2016), *Improved classical simulation of quantum circuits dominated by Clifford gates*, arXiv:1601.07601.

title: Optimal asymptotic magic-state conversion rates
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Determine optimal conversion and distillation rates between specified nonstabilizer states under explicit allowed operations, with and without catalysts.
status: Monotones, protocols, and irreversibility results constrain rates; they do not provide a universal rate formula.
why: Quantifies the irreducible resource cost of non-Clifford computation.
key_works: *Irreversibility of bound magic states assisted by catalysis* (2026), DOI:10.1103/yj6l-lhph; Michael Zurel and Jack Davis (2026), *Basis-independent stabilizerness and maximally noisy magic states*, arXiv:2602.22336.

title: The general multipartite quantum entropy cone
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Characterize all homogeneous entropy inequalities and achievable entropy vectors for general four-party and larger quantum states.
status: Stabilizer-state cones and other restricted families are better understood than the unrestricted quantum cone.
why: Governs possible information-sharing patterns and constrains coding and communication protocols.
key_works: Noah Linden, František Matúš, Mary Beth Ruskai, and Andreas Winter (2013), *The Quantum Entropy Cone of Stabiliser States*, arXiv:1302.5453.

title: Experimentally accessible universality of monitored transitions
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Determine when measurable transport or correlation transitions faithfully diagnose measurement-induced entanglement transitions, including noise, finite size, and nonintegrable dynamics.
status: A 2026 spin-chain study links ballistic–diffusive behavior to entanglement transitions; a broad experimentally robust equivalence is not established.
why: Could expose otherwise postselection-heavy many-body phenomena through accessible observables.
key_works: K. G. S. H. Gunawardana, Ali G. Moghaddam, and Teemu Ojanen (2026), *Postselection-free ballistic-diffusive transition in monitored spin chains*, arXiv:2605.27350.

title: Error-corrected sensing with finite-speed imperfect control
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Quantify and demonstrate the metrological advantage remaining when correction operations have finite duration, noisy ancillas, imperfect gates, and realistic resource costs.
status: Idealized conditions for Heisenberg scaling with error correction are established; physical correction overhead changes the attainable advantage.
why: Tests whether computing-grade control can improve sensors outside ideal limits.
key_works: Sisi Zhou, Mengzhen Zhang, John Preskill, and Liang Jiang (2018), *Achieving the Heisenberg limit in quantum metrology using quantum error correction*, arXiv:1706.02445.

title: Multiparameter sensing with incompatible correction requirements
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Determine achievable precision regions when several parameters must be estimated and preserving one signal conflicts with correcting noise or measuring another.
status: Single-parameter correctability criteria do not fully characterize multiparameter tradeoffs under realistic controls.
why: Real sensors often need vector fields, frequencies, or several coupled physical parameters.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2018), *Achieving the Heisenberg limit in quantum metrology using quantum error correction*, arXiv:1706.02445.

title: Public rare-event syndrome archives
open: Build a versioned, cross-platform dataset containing raw syndrome streams, rare bursts, leakage flags, calibration history, and enough metadata to reproduce logical-failure analyses.
status: Proposed infrastructure target. Published demonstrations provide valuable data, but the target is a sustained interoperable archive, not a single supplementary dataset.
why: Rare logical failures are difficult to study from averaged metrics.
key_works: Google Quantum AI (2025), *Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold*; McEwen et al. (2022), *Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays*.

title: Longitudinal quantum-hardware drift benchmarks
open: Release repeated measurements over operationally meaningful periods, with interventions and missingness recorded, so drift prediction and adaptive control can be evaluated prospectively.
status: Proposed benchmark target; snapshots and selectively reported recalibration improvements do not supply this evaluation.
why: Enables honest testing of controllers and decoders under changing hardware.
key_works: Berritta et al. (2026), *Real-Time Adaptive Tracking of Fluctuating Relaxation Rates*; Bausch et al. (2024), *Learning high-accuracy error decoding for quantum processors*.

title: Comparable logical-computation benchmarks
open: Define and maintain tasks that compare logical throughput and reliability across code families while including rejected runs, decoding, factories, and classical feedback.
status: Proposed infrastructure target beyond physical gate counts and memory-only demonstrations.
why: Makes “logical qubit” claims comparable across architectures.
key_works: Thomas Lubinski et al. (2023), *Application-Oriented Performance Benchmarks for Quantum Computing*, arXiv:2110.03137; Bravyi et al. (2024), *High-threshold and low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum memory*.

title: Hidden-test application benchmarks with matched classical baselines
open: Maintain application suites with frozen specifications, held-out instances, independent classical optimization, and complete quantum preprocessing and readout costs.
status: Proposed benchmark target. Application-oriented benchmarks exist, but benchmark validity must survive continuing classical improvements.
why: Prevents handpicked instances and stale baselines from masquerading as advantage.
key_works: Lubinski et al. (2023), *Application-Oriented Performance Benchmarks for Quantum Computing*, arXiv:2110.03137; Tindall et al. (2024), *Efficient tensor network simulation of IBM’s Eagle kicked Ising experiment*.

title: An adversarial classical-simulation challenge archive
open: Preserve claimed advantage instances, exact scoring rules, computational budgets, subsequent classical attacks, and reproducible outcomes in a continuously updated archive.
status: Proposed infrastructure target motivated by demonstrations whose classical baselines changed after publication.
why: Turns classical progress into cumulative evidence rather than disconnected rebuttals.
key_works: Tindall et al. (2024), *Efficient tensor network simulation of IBM’s Eagle kicked Ising experiment*, arXiv:2306.14887; Cross et al. (2019), *Validating quantum computers using randomized model circuits*.

title: Energy per correct answer datasets
open: Measure complete facility and computation energy per statistically valid answer, including cooling, controls, decoding, rejected runs, and amortized calibration.
status: Proposed measurement target. Full-stack resource models exist; hardware-only power figures do not measure this quantity.
why: Allows credible comparison with classical accelerators and alternative quantum architectures.
key_works: Fellous-Asiani et al. (2023), *Optimizing resource efficiencies for scalable full-stack quantum computers*, arXiv:2209.05469.

title: Reproducible negative-result repositories
open: Archive failed scaling attempts, unsuccessful mitigation, unstable calibrations, and adverse fabrication runs with sufficient methods and metadata for reuse.
status: Proposed infrastructure target; ordinary publication incentives do not automatically produce such a balanced record.
why: Prevents repeated dead ends and selection-biased engineering models.
key_works: de Leon et al. (2021), *Materials challenges and opportunities for quantum computing hardware*; Cai et al. (2023), *Quantum Error Mitigation*.

title: Chemistry benchmarks with independently controlled uncertainty
open: Create benchmark families whose geometry, Hamiltonian, active space, reference uncertainty, and scientifically relevant outputs are explicitly versioned and independently checked.
status: Proposed infrastructure target extending existing resource studies and electronic-structure comparisons.
why: Avoids comparing quantum numerical error against an uncertain or changing chemical target.
key_works: Lee et al. (2022/2023), *Is there evidence for exponential quantum advantage in quantum chemistry?*; von Burg et al. (2021), *Quantum computing enhanced computational catalysis*.

title: Data-access and QRAM cost benchmarks
open: Standardize reporting of coherent-memory construction, updates, query fidelity, classical preprocessing, and amortization assumptions in quantum algorithm evaluations.
status: Proposed benchmark target addressing a recurring mismatch between oracle complexity and physical implementation.
why: Makes claimed data-processing speedups comparable under honest access models.
key_works: Giovannetti, Lloyd, and Maccone (2008), *Quantum random access memory*, arXiv:0708.1879; Tang (2019), *A quantum-inspired classical algorithm for recommendation systems*.

title: Cross-vendor reproducibility of physical and logical metrics
open: Establish executable protocols that reproduce reported metrics across providers while preserving raw outcomes, calibration context, exclusion rules, and uncertainty.
status: Proposed infrastructure target; common metric names do not guarantee common experimental procedures.
why: Enables meaningful procurement, research comparison, and replication.
key_works: Cross et al. (2019), *Validating quantum computers using randomized model circuits*, arXiv:1811.12926; Lubinski et al. (2023), *Application-Oriented Performance Benchmarks for Quantum Computing*.

title: Sustained independent replication funding
open: Establish funding mechanisms that pay independent teams to reproduce full-stack claims, publish adverse findings, and maintain verification capability across hardware generations.
status: Proposed funding-design problem. DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative already includes independent validation; the broader need is sustained, accessible replication rather than absence of all programs.
why: Expensive verification should not depend entirely on the organization making the claim.
key_works: DARPA (2024), *Moving Quantum Computing from Hype to Prototype*; DARPA, *Quantum Benchmarking Initiative*.

title: Durable research access to useful quantum testbeds
open: Provide predictable multiyear access, technical support, raw-data rights, and reproducibility guarantees for researchers who cannot own or privately negotiate access to leading systems.
status: Proposed access-and-funding target. Programs such as NSF’s National Quantum Virtual Laboratory are partial institutional responses.
why: Short promotional access windows are poorly suited to longitudinal hardware science.
key_works: NSF (2024), *NSF National Quantum Virtual Laboratory advances with first five projects*; NSF, *Quantum Information Science*.

title: Open fabrication access and reusable process qualification
open: Fund shared fabrication runs, documented process interfaces, and independently reusable qualification data without requiring each research group to recreate an entire manufacturing stack.
status: Proposed institutional target. Manufacturing-focused quantum hubs exist, but broad access and portable process knowledge require explicit arrangements.
why: Reduces duplication and enables reproducible hardware research.
key_works: U.S. Economic Development Administration, *The Bloch Quantum Tech Hub*; de Leon et al. (2021), *Materials challenges and opportunities for quantum computing hardware*.

title: Maintenance funding for critical open quantum software
open: Create durable support for decoders, compilers, verification tools, and benchmark infrastructure after their initial research grants end, with explicit ownership and compatibility commitments.
status: Proposed funding target; publishing a research implementation is not a maintenance model.
why: Unmaintained infrastructure can invalidate or strand otherwise useful research.
key_works: Hietala et al. (2020), *A Verified Optimizer for Quantum Circuits*; Lubinski et al. (2023), *Application-Oriented Performance Benchmarks for Quantum Computing*; NSF, *Quantum Information Science*.

title: Quantum technician and manufacturing workforce pipelines
open: Determine and fund training pathways that demonstrably supply the cryogenic, photonic, fabrication, packaging, and control skills needed for sustained operation at scale.
status: Current public strategies acknowledge quantum-related skills gaps; the unresolved target is measured training-to-deployment effectiveness.
why: Scaling requires technicians and manufacturing expertise, not only additional theoretical researchers.
key_works: NSF (2026), *NSF FY 2026–2030 Strategic Plan*; U.S. EDA, *The Bloch Quantum Tech Hub*.

title: Independently verified economically useful quantum computation
open: Demonstrate a consequential computation whose independently assessed value exceeds its complete quantum-system cost and the cost of the strongest credible classical alternative.
status: Explicit system-level target, not synonymous with sampling advantage or a favorable asymptotic runtime. DARPA’s benchmarking program uses a related utility-scale criterion.
why: Establishes quantum computing as an economically productive capability.
key_works: DARPA, *Quantum Benchmarking Initiative*; Babbush et al. (2021), *Focus beyond quadratic speedups for error-corrected quantum advantage*.

title: Hundredfold reduction in usable non-Clifford spacetime cost
open: Proposed target: reduce physical spacetime per delivered non-Clifford logical operation by at least 100× against a frozen, fully specified baseline, at matched failure probability and physical noise.
status: An engineering moonshot, not an established conjecture. Cultivation and addressable-code results provide concrete alternative routes.
why: Non-Clifford resources dominate many important fault-tolerant workloads.
key_works: Gidney et al. (2024), *Magic state cultivation: growing T states as cheap as CNOT gates*, arXiv:2409.17595; He et al. (2025), *Quantum Codes with Addressable and Transversal Non-Clifford Gates*.

title: Tenfold reduction in full-system energy per correct answer
open: Proposed target: achieve at least 10× lower complete-system energy for a fixed validated workload, including cooling, controllers, decoding, calibration, and unsuccessful attempts.
status: Resource-efficiency models identify substantial tradeoffs; a measured complete-system improvement is stronger than a lower-power component.
why: Makes large quantum systems more affordable and physically deployable.
key_works: Fellous-Asiani et al. (2023), *Optimizing resource efficiencies for scalable full-stack quantum computers*, arXiv:2209.05469.

title: Tenfold reduction in delivered high-fidelity entanglement cost
open: Proposed target: lower cost per usable remote Bell pair by 10× at fixed distance, fidelity, and availability, counting hardware, multiplexing, memory, discarded attempts, and operation.
status: Conversion efficiency or raw heralding rate alone does not satisfy this target.
why: Could change the viability of modular quantum computers and repeaters.
key_works: Main et al. (2025), *Distributed Quantum Computing across an Optical Network Link*; Tu et al. (2026), *Quantum-memory-assisted on-demand microwave-optical transduction*.

title: Month-long unattended useful logical service
open: Proposed target: operate useful error-corrected workloads for a month with automatic calibration, component recovery, verified outputs, and an auditable record of downtime and failed jobs.
status: Continuous coherent hardware operation is demonstrated on shorter experimental timescales; service-level logical continuity adds recovery, computation, and verification requirements.
why: Converts a laboratory processor into dependable scientific infrastructure.
key_works: Chiu et al. (2025), *Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system*, arXiv:2506.20660; Google Quantum AI (2025), *Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold*.

title: R10-01. An eleven-qubit, three-logical-qubit code with weight-four checks
open: Determine whether an \([[11,3,3]]\) qubit stabilizer code admits eight independent commuting generators, each of Pauli weight at most four. Allow arbitrary connectivity and non-CSS constructions.
status: The 2026 low-weight-code analysis leaves the minimum possible maximum generator weight at **four or five**. Weight-five constructions exist; weight four remains unresolved.
why: Resolves a small, concrete check-complexity gap relevant to hardware-efficient error correction.
key_works: Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Austin Yubo He, Zimu Li, and Zi-Wen Liu (2026), *Theory of low-weight quantum codes*, arXiv:2601.19848.

title: R10-02. The square-root distance conjecture for weight-four stabilizer codes
open: Prove or refute that every qubit stabilizer code encoding at least one logical qubit and generated by weight-at-most-four checks satisfies \(d=O(\sqrt n)\), **without assuming geometric locality**.
status: Explicitly conjectured in 2026. Weight-three generators impose much stronger limitations; weight-four toric-code families attain square-root distance.
why: Would identify an intrinsic check-weight obstruction, rather than a hardware-layout obstruction.
key_works: Wei et al. (2026), *Theory of low-weight quantum codes*, arXiv:2601.19848.

title: R10-03. An absolutely maximally entangled state of eight ququarts
open: Construct a pure state on \((\mathbb C^4)^{\otimes8}\) whose reduction to every four-party subset is \(I_{256}/256\), or prove that no such state exists.
status: The 2026 classification of seven-party absolutely maximally entangled states explicitly identifies **AME(8,4)** as a remaining existence problem. Settling seven-party cases does not settle this eight-party instance.
why: Supplies—or rules out—a particularly small perfect tensor with applications to erasure correction, secret sharing, and tensor-network constructions.
key_works: Fei Shi, Xiande Zhang, Qi Zhao, and Lvzhou Li (2026), *Complete Existence Classification of Seven-Partite Absolutely Maximally Entangled States*, arXiv:2608.01011.
aliases: AME(8,4); eight-leg perfect tensor of bond dimension four.

title: R10-04. Optimal length of permutation-invariant codes correcting \(t\) errors
open: Determine whether the shortest two-dimensional permutation-invariant qubit code correcting \(t\) arbitrary errors has length
status: The 2026 numerical study conjectures the equivalent distance bound \(n\ge(3d^2+1)/4\), with evidence of saturation. General constructions and numerical optima do not establish the proposed formula for every \(t\).
why: Determines the optimal redundancy when individual particles cannot be distinguished or addressed.
key_works: Liam J. Bond, Jiří Minář, Māris Ozols, Arghavan Safavi-Naini, and Vladyslav Visnevskyi (2026), *Permutation-invariant codes: a numerical study and qudit constructions*, arXiv:2603.10981; Arda Aydin, Max A. Alekseyev, and Alexander Barg (2024), *A family of permutationally invariant quantum codes*, Quantum 8, 1321.

title: R10-05. A seven-qubit code encoding three orthogonal states and correcting one error
open: Determine whether an arbitrary, potentially nonadditive \(((7,3,3))_2\) quantum code exists. Equivalently, find a rank-three projector satisfying all distance-three Knill–Laflamme conditions, or certify impossibility.
status: The March 2026 rational-certificate table still gives **\(2\le K_{\max}(7,3)\le3\)**. The upper endpoint is not known to be achievable.
why: Tests whether abandoning stabilizer structure improves one of the smallest single-error-correcting codes.
key_works: Gerard Anglès Munné and Felix Huber (2026), *SDP bounds on quantum codes: rational certificates*, arXiv:2603.19901.

title: R10-06. A nine-qubit, thirteen-dimensional, distance-three code
open: Construct a \(((9,13,3))_2\) code or prove that every nine-qubit code correcting one arbitrary error has dimension at most twelve. The search must include codes outside the codeword-stabilized framework.
status: A twelve-dimensional nonadditive code is known; the 2026 certified bounds remain **\(12\le K_{\max}(9,3)\le13\)**. Searches restricted to codeword-stabilized constructions do not exclude arbitrary codes.
why: Closes a longstanding one-dimension gap in a canonical nonadditive-code benchmark.
key_works: Sixia Yu, Qing Chen, C. H. Lai, and C. H. Oh (2008), *Nonadditive Quantum Error-Correcting Code*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.090501; A. Rigby, J. C. Olivier, and P. Jarvis (2019), *Heuristic construction of codeword stabilized codes*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevA.100.062303; Anglès Munné and Huber (2026), arXiv:2603.19901.

title: R10-07. Semi-Clifford normal forms for two odd-prime-dimensional qudits
open: Determine whether every two-qudit gate in every finite level of the Clifford hierarchy can be written \(U=C_1DC_2\), with Clifford \(C_1,C_2\) and diagonal \(D\), when the local dimension is an odd prime. The unresolved levels begin beyond the established third-level results.
status: The 2025 one-qubit-or-qudit classification does not settle two-qudit higher levels. Its concluding conjectures explicitly extend the normal-form question to two qudits.
why: Would provide systematic gate-teleportation and synthesis structures for higher-dimensional fault-tolerant computation.
key_works: Nadish de Silva and Oscar Lautsch (2025), *The Clifford hierarchy for one qubit or qudit*, arXiv:2501.07939; I. Chen and N. de Silva (2024), *Characterising semi-Clifford gates using algebraic sets*, Communications in Mathematical Physics 405, 201.

title: R10-08. The exact inscribed ball of the multiqubit stabilizer polytope
open: For \(d=2^n\), determine whether every state satisfying
status: September 2026 work proves the weaker purity threshold \(1/(d-0.458327\ldots)\) and identifies the half-unit constant as the conjectured optimum. This is a geometric threshold, not a magic-state conversion-rate problem.
why: Gives a sharp, basis-independent certificate that sufficiently mixed states contain no magic.
key_works: Z. Liu and Zi-Wen Liu (2026), *On the geometry and typicality of quantum magic*, arXiv:2609.03944; Michael Zurel and Jack Davis (2026), *Basis-independent stabilizerness and maximally noisy magic states*, arXiv:2602.22336.

title: R10-09. The original tensor-product quantum KKL inequality
open: For every Hermitian \(n\)-qubit observable \(A\) with \(A^2=I\), prove a universal bound
status: The original quantum KKL question dates to Montanaro–Osborne. Recent Talagrand, random-restriction, and modified-influence inequalities provide important alternatives, rather than settling this precise \(L_2\)-influence formulation.
why: Would show that a nontrivial quantum Boolean observable must depend detectably on some physical qubit.
key_works: Ashley Montanaro and Tobias J. Osborne (2008/2010), *Quantum boolean functions*, arXiv:0810.2435; Yong Jiao, Wenlong Lin, Sijie Luo, and Dejian Zhou (2024), *Quantum KKL-type Inequalities Revisited*, arXiv:2411.12399.

title: R10-10. Aaronson–Ambainis influence for all bounded low-degree polynomials
open: Prove or refute that every bounded multilinear polynomial \(p:\{-1,1\}^N\to[0,1]\), of degree at most \(d\) and variance at least \(\varepsilon\), has a coordinate of influence at least \((\varepsilon/d)^C\) for some universal constant \(C\).
status: Still open generally. September 2026 results obtain sharp inequalities for completely bounded polynomials and associated quantum algorithms; those additional structural assumptions do not cover every bounded polynomial.
why: Would explain why substantial quantum query advantages require exploitable structure rather than merely low polynomial degree.
key_works: Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis (2014), *The Need for Structure in Quantum Speedups*, Theory of Computing 10, 133–166; Francisco Escudero Gutiérrez, Miquel Saucedo, and Carlos Palazuelos (2026), *Optimal inequalities for completely bounded polynomials and the limitations of quantum query algorithms*, arXiv:2609.05201.

title: R10-11. Exact parity in higher-depth QAC⁰
open: Determine whether polynomial-size, constant-depth quantum circuits built from arbitrary one-qubit gates and unbounded-fanin Toffoli gates can compute parity exactly using polynomially many initialized ancillas. Unbounded fanout must not be supplied as a free primitive.
status: The 2025–2026 lower-bound work excludes exact parity at depth three even with unrestricted size and ancillas, and establishes approximation limitations at depth two. General higher constant depth remains unresolved.
why: Resolves whether genuinely quantum interference defeats the classical constant-depth obstruction to parity in this gate model.
key_works: Cristopher Moore (1999), *Quantum Circuits: Fanout, Parity, and Counting*; Malvika Raj Joshi, Avishay Tal, Francisca Vasconcelos, and John Wright (2025/2026), *Improved Lower Bounds for QAC0*, arXiv:2512.14643; DOI:10.1145/3798129.3800922.

title: R10-12. Unrestricted lower bounds for finding a welded-tree path
open: Prove an exponential quantum-query lower bound for outputting an explicit entrance-to-exit path in the standard randomly welded-tree oracle problem, or find a substantially faster path-output algorithm.
status: Quantum walks can find the exit efficiently without retaining a path. The 2023 “power of forgetting” result establishes a separation for a restricted class of genuine, rooted algorithms; the unrestricted path-finding question remains stronger.
why: Separates learning that an endpoint is reachable from producing an inspectable classical witness of reachability.
key_works: Andrew M. Childs, Matthew Coudron, and Amin Shiraz Gilani (2023), *Quantum algorithms and the power of forgetting*, arXiv:2211.12447; Scott Aaronson (2021), *Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity*, arXiv:2109.06917.

title: R10-13. The PPT-squared conjecture beyond established special cases
open: Determine whether the composition of any two positive-partial-transpose quantum channels is entanglement breaking. A counterexample must give two valid PPT channels whose composition retains entanglement with a reference.
status: Qutrit and other structured cases are established. An August 2026 preprint reports finite entanglement-breaking index for every PPT channel, but eventual destruction under repeated composition is weaker than destruction after two PPT stages.
why: Determines how quickly successive bound-entanglement-compatible noise processes destroy all transmissible entanglement.
key_works: Sang-Jun Park (2026), *Every PPT channel has finite entanglement breaking index*, arXiv:2608.13551; Junhyeong An and Soojoon Lee (2026), *Beyond the Positive Partial Transpose Squared Conjecture: The Qutrit Case*, arXiv:2607.15947.

title: R10-14. Absolute PPT versus absolute separability for two qutrits
open: Determine whether every \(3\times3\) bipartite state that remains PPT after every global unitary also remains separable after every global unitary.
status: Open for two qutrits. March 2026 work classifies relevant extreme points with three distinct eigenvalues, but does not establish equality of the full absolutely-PPT and absolutely-separable sets.
why: Tests whether the spectrum alone can conceal entanglement beyond all partial-transpose tests, even after arbitrary global basis changes.
key_works: Nalan Wang, Lin Chen, and Zhiwei Song (2026), *Extreme points of absolutely PPT states with exactly three distinct eigenvalues*, arXiv:2603.20717.

title: R10-15. Essential tensor-stable positive maps over ordinary complex numbers
open: Construct a finite-dimensional complex-linear map \(\Phi\) such that \(\Phi^{\otimes n}\) is positive for every positive integer \(n\), while \(\Phi\) is neither completely positive nor completely copositive; alternatively, prove none exist.
status: Nontrivial positivity for any prescribed finite number of tensor powers is possible. Constructions using nonstandard hypercomplex numbers do not settle existence over ordinary \(\mathbb C\).
why: Would clarify whether positivity can remain stable under unlimited composition without arising from the familiar completely positive structures.
key_works: Alexander Müller-Hermes, David Reeb, and Michael M. Wolf (2015), *Positivity of linear maps under tensor powers*, arXiv:1502.05630; Mirte van der Eyden, Tim Netzer, and Gemma De las Cuevas (2022), *Halos and undecidability of tensor stable positive maps*, arXiv:2110.02113.

title: R10-16. Decidability of tensor-stable positivity
open: Given an exactly specified finite-dimensional map with rational complex coefficients, decide whether all its tensor powers are positive, or prove that no algorithm can decide this for every input.
status: The 2022 analysis proves undecidability for a related matrix-multiplication-tensor positivity problem and develops connections to tensor-stable maps. It does not settle the ordinary all-tensor-powers decision problem.
why: Determines whether a complete automated classifier for this channel-related positivity property is possible.
key_works: Mirte van der Eyden, Tim Netzer, and Gemma De las Cuevas (2022), *Halos and undecidability of tensor stable positive maps*, arXiv:2110.02113; DOI:10.1088/1751-8121/ac726e.

title: R10-17. Equal-weight, low-Kraus-rank decomposition of every qutrit channel
open: Determine whether every qutrit-to-qutrit channel admits
status: July 2026 work proves strong decomposition results for qubit-input channels and several other classes, together with a weaker qutrit statement. The equal-weight qutrit case remains a concrete unresolved instance of the strong conjecture.
why: Would bound the environment size needed in each branch of a uniformly randomized channel implementation.
key_works: Niranjan Kumar and Michael M. Wolf (2026), *The Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture & equipartitions of positive operators*, arXiv:2607.23066; Mary Beth Ruskai (2007), *Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory*, arXiv:0708.1902.

title: R10-18. Joint dimension–accuracy optimality of diamond-norm channel tomography
open: Determine the sharp number of ordinary forward queries needed to learn an arbitrary noisy \(d\)-dimensional channel to diamond-norm error \(\varepsilon\). In particular, decide whether the general \(O(d^4/\varepsilon^2)\) dependence is jointly optimal when ancillas, collective measurements, and adaptive strategies are allowed.
status: The 2026 revision establishes optimal dimension and Kraus-rank dependence at constant accuracy, with upper bound \(O(d_{\rm in}d_{\rm out}k/\varepsilon^2)\). Matching separate parameter bounds do not automatically establish a matching joint lower bound.
why: Fixes the fundamental experimental cost of learning worst-case channel behavior rather than selected average observables.
key_works: Antonio Anna Mele and Lennart Bittel (2025/2026), *Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance*, arXiv:2512.10214.

title: R10-19. Finite collapse of the exact PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy
open: Prove or refute Conjecture S33 of Lami–Mele–Regula:
status: The 2025 paper establishes efficient approximation through converging hierarchies and reports numerical support for collapse. Approximate computability is already established; universal exact collapse is not.
why: Would remove the remaining hierarchy limit from an operational entanglement-cost formula.
key_works: Ludovico Lami, Francesco A. Mele, and Bartosz Regula (2025), *Computable entanglement cost under positive partial transpose operations*, arXiv:2405.09613; Physical Review Letters 134, 090202, Supplemental Material, Conjecture S33.

title: R10-20. Sub-ebit implementation of the elegant joint measurement
open: Can a higher-Schmidt-rank pure resource state with entanglement entropy below one ebit implement the two-qubit elegant joint measurement exactly and deterministically by LOCC? Only its classical outcome must be produced.
status: One ebit suffices by teleportation. The 2026 analysis explicitly leaves the higher-rank, sub-ebit possibility open.
why: Tests whether extra resource dimension lowers the entanglement cost of a fixed distributed measurement.
key_works: Seiseki Akibue, Jisho Miyazaki, and Hiroyuki Osaka (2025/2026), *Optimizing Entanglement Manipulation via Algebraic-Geometric Decompositions and Semidefinite Programming Hierarchies*, arXiv:2501.17394.
aliases: EJM cost; symmetric joint measurement cost.

title: R10-21. A strict asymptotic distillation gap between SEP and PPT operations
open: Exhibit a bipartite state \(\rho\) for which \(D_{\rm SEP}(\rho)<D_{\rm PPT}(\rho)\), using asymptotic singlet rates with vanishing error. A single-copy success-probability gap is insufficient.
status: The 2026 analysis explicitly identifies this separation as unresolved despite progress on single-copy optimization.
why: Would show that the PPT relaxation overestimates asymptotically usable entanglement even relative to all separable operations.
key_works: Akibue, Miyazaki, and Osaka (2025/2026), *Optimizing Entanglement Manipulation via Algebraic-Geometric Decompositions and Semidefinite Programming Hierarchies*, arXiv:2501.17394, Section 5.5.

title: R10-22. The joint large-dimension crossover of optimal port-based teleportation
open: For optimal deterministic port-based teleportation, determine whether
status: The 2026 correspondence with unitary estimation establishes sharp \(d^4/N^2\)-order infidelity in the appropriate asymptotic regime and exact small-port cases. These do not determine the full crossover function when ports and dimension grow together.
why: Quantifies teleportation overhead precisely in the regime where port counts first become comparable to the squared system dimension.
key_works: Satoshi Yoshida, Yuki Koizumi, Michał Studziński, Marco Túlio Quintino, and Mio Murao (2026), *One-to-One Correspondence between Deterministic Port-Based Teleportation and Unitary Estimation*, arXiv:2408.11902; DOI:10.1109/TIT.2026.3658543.

title: R10-23. Efficient capacity-achieving HSW square-root decoding
open: Construct efficiently described capacity-achieving codes for general finite classical–quantum memoryless channels whose Holevo–Schumacher–Westmoreland square-root decoding measurement has a polynomial-size implementation. Charge for codeword-state preparation, block encoding, conditioning, and measurement synthesis rather than assuming an exponential codebook oracle.
status: The coding theorem establishes existence of good measurements, not efficient circuits. Algorithms for Petz recovery and pretty-good measurements provide implementations under access and conditioning assumptions that need not remain efficient for HSW code families.
why: Converts a communication-capacity theorem into an executable receiver architecture.
key_works: Mark M. Wilde (2017), *Quantum Information Theory*, second edition, Section 20.3; András Gilyén, Seth Lloyd, Iman Marvian, Yihui Quek, and Mark M. Wilde (2022), *Quantum algorithm for Petz recovery channels and pretty good measurements*, arXiv:2006.16924; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.220502.

title: R10-24. An unrestricted strong converse for blind mixed-state compression
open: For an arbitrary finite-dimensional source \(\rho^{AR}\), prove that reference-preserving reconstruction fidelity tends to zero whenever the compression rate is below \(S(CQ)\), where \(C,Q\) are the nonredundant Koashi–Imoto components. Allow arbitrary encoding and decoding channels.
status: The optimal first-order rate is established. The 2025 strong-converse revision proves results under additional decoder assumptions, rather than the unrestricted statement.
why: Determines whether operating below the fundamental rate causes complete failure, rather than merely preventing fidelity from approaching one.
key_works: Zahra Baghali Khanian and Andreas Winter (2022), *General Mixed State Quantum Data Compression with and without Entanglement Assistance*, arXiv:1912.08506; Zahra Baghali Khanian (2022; revised 2025), *Strong Converse Bounds for Compression of Mixed States*, arXiv:2206.09415.

title: R10-25. Continuity at one of regularized Rényi entanglement of purification
status: Exponential strong-converse bounds for visible compression hold below the left-hand threshold. Identifying it with the operational threshold on the right remains conditional on this continuity statement.
why: Resolves a limit-interchange obstruction in visible quantum source coding.
key_works: Zahra Baghali Khanian (2022; revised 2025), *Strong Converse Bounds for Compression of Mixed States*, arXiv:2206.09415.

title: R10-26. The entropy photon-number inequality for arbitrary independent inputs
open: For independent \(n\)-mode inputs \(A,B\) mixed on a beamsplitter of transmissivity \(\eta\), prove
status: Conjectured in 2007 and still discussed as open in a June 2026 specialist symposium. The established quantum entropy-power inequality and one-mode Gaussian optimizer theorems do not establish this full arbitrary-input statement.
why: Would provide sharp entropy constraints for optical mixing and strengthen capacity analyses of bosonic communication systems.
key_works: Giacomo De Palma, Andrea Mari, and Vittorio Giovannetti (2014), *A generalization of the Entropy Power Inequality to Bosonic Quantum Systems*, arXiv:1402.0404; Giacomo De Palma, Dario Trevisan, and Vittorio Giovannetti (2017), *Gaussian States Minimize the Output Entropy of One-Mode Quantum Gaussian Channels*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.160503.

title: R10-27. Minimum-output-entropy additivity with a nonunital qubit factor
status: Unital-qubit results and several other special classes are established. High-dimensional counterexamples to general additivity do not answer this qubit-factor question.
why: Identifies whether a single noisy qubit channel can participate in the entangled-input mechanisms responsible for entropy nonadditivity.
key_works: Christopher King (2002), *Additivity for unital qubit channels*, Journal of Mathematical Physics 43, 4641–4653; Alexander S. Holevo (2015), *Gaussian optimizers and the additivity problem in quantum information theory*, arXiv:1501.00652.

title: R10-28. Intermediate-\(p\) multiplicativity for identity-mixed Werner–Holevo channels
status: Multiplicativity at \(p=2\) is proved for the mixed family; the unmixed Werner–Holevo channel is understood for \(1\le p\le2\). These endpoint and boundary results do not cover the stated interior region.
why: Isolates a highly symmetric surviving test case after broad maximal-output-norm conjectures failed.
key_works: Spiros Michalakis (2007), *Multiplicativity of the maximal output 2-norm for depolarized Werner-Holevo channels*, arXiv:0707.1722; Nilanjana Datta (2004), *Multiplicativity of Maximal p-Norms in Werner-Holevo Channels for \(1\le p\le2\)*, arXiv:quant-ph/0410063.

title: R10-29. A strict advantage of fully interleaved superchannel discrimination
open: In the realization-based superchannel-discrimination model, determine whether fully general causal interleaving can achieve a strictly better asymmetric error exponent than nested adaptive strategies. Supply an explicit pair exhibiting a gap, or prove equality under clearly stated access rules.
status: Hirche establishes achievable and converse quantities for several strategy classes, but leaves gaps between the general interleaved and more restricted formulations. Classical cases do not settle the quantum question.
why: Determines whether access to a process’s temporal structure has operational value beyond repeated use of the process as a single higher-order object.
key_works: Christoph Hirche (2023), *Quantum Network Discrimination*, arXiv:2103.02404; DOI:10.22331/q-2023-07-25-1064.

title: R10-30. Polynomial entanglement lower bounds for one-round quantum routing
open: Find an explicit efficiently computable Boolean family \(f_n(x,y)\) such that any constant-error, one-round simultaneous-message protocol routing an unknown qubit to the party selected by \(f_n\) requires initial entanglement of formation at least \(n^c\), for some \(c>0\).
status: The September 2026 revision of Bogner’s work proves an **\(\Omega(\log n)\)** entanglement-of-formation lower bound for inner-product routing, allowing arbitrary mixed shared resources and error at most \(0.09\). Polynomial lower bounds remain open.
why: Would establish substantial resource requirements for nonlocal quantum computation and strengthen the foundations of position-based cryptographic security.
key_works: Kevin Bogner (2026), *Robust logarithmic entanglement lower bound for f-routing*, arXiv:2608.05775v3; René Allerstorfer, Harry Buhrman, Alex May, Florian Speelman, and Philip Verduyn Lunel (2024), *Relating Non-Local Quantum Computation to Information Theoretic Cryptography*, Quantum 8, 1387.

title: R10-31. Causally faithful routed-circuit decompositions
open: Determine whether every finite-dimensional unitary admits a routed-circuit representation in which the absence of a permitted directed route exactly captures each operational no-influence relation. If not, characterize the obstruction and exhibit a minimal counterexample.
status: The September 2026 lattice-theoretic characterization advances ordinary unitary causal decompositions. Universal faithful realization using the richer routed-circuit formalism remains a separate target, also developed through thesis and workshop work.
why: Would connect experimentally meaningful causal independence to compositional circuit structure without introducing fictitious causal paths.
key_works: Tein van der Lugt and Robin Lorenz (2026), *Unitary causal decompositions: a characterisation via lattice theory*, arXiv:2508.11762; DOI:10.22331/q-2026-09-30-2218. Tein van der Lugt (2025), *Causal and Compositional Structure in Quantum Theory*, doctoral thesis, DOI:10.5287/ORA-VQ7OPD7AP. Augustin Vanrietvelde, Hlér Kristjánsson, and Jonathan Barrett (2021), *Routed Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:2011.08120.

title: R10-32. Infinite coherence cost without pairwise reversibility
open: Determine whether a Gibbs-preserving channel can require unbounded coherence for exact implementation by thermal operations even though it is **not pairwise reversible**—that is, no recovery channel can exactly restore any pair of orthogonal input states. Construct such a channel or prove that pairwise reversibility is necessary for divergent coherence cost.
status: Tajima–Takagi prove infinite coherence cost for a class of pairwise-reversible channels satisfying an additional energy-related condition. Their final 2025 paper explicitly leaves open whether every cost-diverging Gibbs-preserving channel must be pairwise reversible.
why: Identifies the physical mechanism behind thermodynamic operations that appear mathematically free but cannot be implemented with finite coherence resources.
key_works: Hiroyasu Tajima and Ryuji Takagi (2025), *Gibbs-Preserving Operations Requiring Infinite Amount of Quantum Coherence*, arXiv:2404.03479; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.170201.
